text: Parenting experts say children need to learn independence and resilience. <break time="0.8s" /> But cities and suburbs do not offer safe walk and bike routes to school, malls kick teenagers out on the weekends, and free time disappears under a spreadsheet of activities. <break time="0.8s" /> All of those musts take more of the parents time or money to navigate, because the child cannot do it on their own. <break time="0.8s" /> As Darby Saxbe, a clinical psychologist, recently wrote in the New York Times, underparenting requires structural change. <break time="0.8s" /> Unlike most political experts, she is not just talking about economic policies like family leave and government supported childcare. <break time="0.8s" /> She is talking about actual physical structures, and the cultural change required to populate them. <break time="0.8s" /> We need to build back our tolerance for children in public spaces, she writes, and create safe environments where lightly supervised kids can move around freely. <break time="0.8s" /> To help parents raise independent children, cities and suburbs need to create supportive environments, where parents can keep their children under mild supervision, through changes in physical structure and culture.
